# Best RV power station and solar combo

The best pick depends on how you camp, mainly whether you need to run a roof air conditioner. The results didn't include direct product pages for most of these, so the links below go to the reviews that cover each one, and those pages have the current buy buttons. Prices change, so check them before you buy.

## Pick by RV use

**Weekends and light use (fridge, lights, laptop, Starlink): Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**
- It has 1,070Wh, 1,500W output and weighs about 23.8 lb.
- Solar input tops out at 400W, so two 200W Jackery SolarSaga panels use all of it.
- It's simple, but it can't take an add-on battery. ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))

**Longer trips, with room to grow: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus**
- It has 1,024Wh, 1,800W output and 1,000W of solar input across two 500W inputs.
- It expands to 5kWh, and the source rates it the best overall camping pick.
- You need two panel connections to reach the full solar input, but a single 200W panel will still charge it, just more slowly. ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))

**Roof AC or boondocking: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 or Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro**
- The DELTA Pro 3 has 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous output and 8,000W surge, and expands past 12kWh.
- The Jackery 3000 Pro has 3,024Wh and 3,000W continuous with 6,000W surge, enough to start a 13,500 BTU AC without a soft-start kit.
- A 13,500 BTU AC draws about 1,500W running and spikes past 3,000W at startup, so a 1,000W unit won't work. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))
- Both units are heavy, and the DELTA Pro 3 is a two-person lift.

**Mid-range value with an RV port: BLUETTI AC200L**
- It has 2,048Wh, 2,400W output, 1,200W solar input and a built-in 30A RV outlet.
- It weighs about 62 lb. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/), [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))

**Big capacity per dollar: ALLPOWERS R4000**
- It has 3,456Wh, 3,600W at 120V, an RV outlet, and 2,000W of solar input over three inputs.
- It has a 5-year warranty and weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it's more of a fixed install.
- The list price is $1,499. Code EXTRA12 takes it to about $1,319 and expires 2026-11-15.
- [Buy at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh))

## Solar panels

- **Match panels to the unit's solar input limit.** Extra panel wattage beyond the limit does nothing. For example, the Jackery 1000 v2 caps at 400W.
- **For small units,** a 200W foldable panel such as the Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase is a common pairing. ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife))
- **For a roof array on a larger unit,** check the voltage and current limits of each input before buying panels.
- **Allow for sun conditions.** A 300–400W array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))

## My recommendation

- **Most RVers without AC:** EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus plus a 200W+ panel setup, for the expandability and solar headroom.
- **Lightest and simplest:** Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 with two SolarSaga 200W panels.
- **AC off-grid:** DELTA Pro 3 or Jackery 3000 Pro.

Before buying, add up your watt-hours per day. A 150W fridge over 10 hours is about 1,500Wh. Also check whether you'll run a large appliance, since that sets the minimum output you need. Hardwiring into the RV's electrical system should be done by a licensed electrician.

If you tell me your RV type, your daily loads and whether you have an AC, I can narrow this to one combo.
